_meta.title: Maturity structure of marketable Treasury debt
_meta.source: Treasury Monthly Statement of the Public Debt (instrument composition, May 2026); Joint Economic Committee monthly debt update (Jun 2026 average maturity)
notes: The 30-year bond is the longest instrument issued, so nothing outstanding today was issued before 1996.
But average maturity is about 71 months, roughly six years. Roughly a third of debt matures within twelve months.
This is why rate rises after 2021 repriced the whole stock within a few years. It is the causal link to the net interest chart.
Savings bonds (Series EE and I) reach final maturity at 20-30 years and are non-marketable; excluded from these figures.

Bills, notes and bonds are three of the marketable instrument families, not all of them. They sum to about $28.1T against a $30.9T marketable total; the $2.8T difference is mostly Treasury Inflation-Protected Securities and floating-rate notes, plus a small Federal Financing Bank balance, which this chart does not draw. The bills share_pct is the published 22 and reconciles with amount_t / marketable_total_t (21.9); geometry still comes from amount_t and the percentage only from the curated field, so no component derives a share.

history_months is a four-point maturity time series and is deliberately NOT charted. sections.md is explicit that this section is not built as a time series; the field is kept in the data for reference but no component may reference it.
